title: Metronome for Corgi
statementMd:
Azora the corgi loves music but cannot catch the rhythm well, especially when counting beats! After hard research on music theory, Azora found a hidden theorem: There won't be a note crossing the boundary between the beats for modern songs (or for most barking sessions for that matter).

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/fb1367b0b15c438a5a44b27ac1a4c1b8c75792da.png)

To simplify the problem, we assume that a modern song consists of several sequential notes whose lengths are 𝑙1,𝑙2,⋯,𝑙𝑛l1,l2,⋯,ln milliseconds. The notes will be played one by one, which means the song will start playing the first note at time 00, and the second note at the beginning of the 𝑙1+1l1+1 milliseconds, and the third note at the beginning of the 𝑙1+𝑙2+1l1+l2+1 milliseconds, and so on.

If the length of the beat is 𝐿L milliseconds, then there should not exist any note that is playing but not starting to play at the beginning of the 𝑘𝐿kL milliseconds, for any non-negative integer 𝑘k. Formally, there should not exist any note 𝑖i such that ∑𝑖−1𝑗=1𝑙𝑗<𝑘𝐿∑j=1i−1lj<kL but ∑𝑖𝑗=1𝑙𝑗>𝑘𝐿∑j=1ilj>kL for any non-negative integer 𝑘k.

Now Azora has received a new song from her humans, and she wants to practice counting beats before she barks the song back to them. To challenge herself, Azora wants to find the smallest possible length of a beat, such that it satisfies the theorem. Can you help her?

## Input

The first line contains a single integer 𝑛 (1≤𝑛≤2×105)n (1≤n≤2×105), representing the number of notes in the song.

The second line contains 𝑛n integers 𝑙1,𝑙2,⋯,𝑙𝑛 (1≤𝑙𝑖≤109)l1,l2,⋯,ln (1≤li≤109), representing the length of each note.

## Output

Output a single integer, representing the minimum possible length of a beat.
